item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ can all be in SCOPe family a.298.1.1 because TAL effectors are repeat proteins: the homologous structural unit is the all-alpha TAL-effector repeat, and different PDB chains contain different numbers of tandem copies of that repeat. In the SCOPe hierarchy this places them in class a, fold a.298, superfamily a.298.1, and the close TAL effector family a.298.1.1; the family assignment reflects common ancestry and the same repeating two-helix architecture, not comparable full-chain lengths or a fixed number of residues. The length differences therefore mostly report repeat copy number, truncation/construct boundaries, and engineered or natural array size. They should not be used as if the domains were one-to-one globular homologs over their entire residue ranges: insertions/deletions of whole repeats must be modeled, representative selection should avoid treating every repeat array length as an independent fold, and DNA-base specificity or effector function cannot be transferred solely from the SCOPe family label because TAL specificity depends on the order of repeat-variable diresidues in the array.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
